title: Topology-aware async TP/PP stall reconstruction
content:
Context:
We keep seeing sporadic p99 spikes (~2.5-3x baseline) on a mix of customer traces that exercise mid-length context (2k-4k tokens) with replicated model instances using async tensor parallel (TP) + pipeline parallel (PP) combos.

High-level hypothesis:
There is a topology-sensitive interaction between async TP scheduling and PP micro-synchronizations that creates short-lived NIC/memory bursts and NCCL collective reconfiguration events, which amplify packetization overheads and cause tail latency. The problem is most visible when:
- shards are placed across heterogeneous NVLink/PCIe hops (some intra-node NVLink, some cross-node PCIe via NIC)
- request mixes contain a small fraction of long sequences that extend KV cache usage and trigger partial KV cache replays
- async TP attempts to overlap comm+compute by issuing collectives opportunistically, increasing small-packet allreduce frequency

What we reconstructed (quick summary of experiments):
1) Trace-driven replay: played 12 representative customer traces through synthetic harness with topology mapping variants (flat NVLink-first, rack-aware, strict intra-node packing). Observed p99 factor change: flat NVLink-first baseline p99=42 ms; cross-node interleaved placement p99=99 ms (2.36x).
2) Microbench set: isolated NCCL allreduce with small 8–64 KB payloads, varied NIC interrupt coalescing and host staging. Cross-node paths showed 40–65% higher tail compared to intra-node for same message size.
3) Async-scheduling toggle: disabled async TP overlap (force lockstep collectives): p99 dropped by ~20% on interleaved placement, but worst-case throughput decreased by 6%.
4) KV cache replay test: enabling replay increased frequency of small prefix collectives; network bursts aligned with cache-refill windows correlated to p99 spikes.

Instrumentation notes (what we used):
- Per-GPU timestamps emitted to host logs (coarse-grained) + inferred latency windows from request->first-token and request->last-token.
- NCCL_TRACE on test cluster (striped) with enhanced timestamps (microsecond resolution).
- Linux ethtool stats + IB counters sampled at 1ms resolution using perf counters + custom user-space sampler to correlate NIC tx bursts with collectives.
- A small eBPF probe to log syscall-level host staging events (cudaMemcpyAsync host<>GPU) with PID and buffer size.

Observations (raw):
- Short, repeated allreduces (~8–16 KB) dominate the high-frequency tail. When these land on cross-node links the queueing delay increases multiplicatively due to packetization + NIC interrupt jitter.
- On topologies with mixed NVLink coverage, async TP tends to schedule neighbouring tensor slices across the best local links but occasionally spans a slice boundary that crosses a PCIe/NIC hop; the resulting collective changes topology mid-epoch and triggers NCCL microreconfig (observed as 1–2 ms hiccups).
- Host staging (GPU-to-host) happens more often than expected for short KV cache replays — likely due to fragmentation of CUDA pinned buffers when memory is near pressure thresholds. Host staging correlates with NIC Tx bursts (same time window).
- Disabling opportunistic async overlap reduces frequency of these small collectives (they batch into larger ones) but increases steady compute stall since overlap benefits are lost.

Representative numbers (median of 5 runs each):
- Baseline packed intra-node placement: p50=9ms, p95=22ms, p99=42ms, throughput=120 qps
- Interleaved cross-node placement: p50=11ms, p95=38ms, p99=99ms, throughput=118 qps
- Interleaved + async overlap disabled: p50=10ms, p95=30ms, p99=79ms, throughput=111 qps
- Interleaved + NIC irq-coalesce tuned (120us -> 60us): p50=10ms, p95=29ms, p99=68ms, throughput=117 qps

Quick root cause sketch:
1) Small, frequent collectives produced by async TP (and prefetched KV replays) exacerbate microburst behavior on cross-node links.
2) Packetization + NIC interrupt machinery cause tail amplification when bursts collide with other tenant traffic or when IRQ coalescing settings are suboptimal.
3) NCCL internal reconfiguration (when topology changes across replicas or ranks move to different link classes) adds unpredictable 0.5–2ms stalls that sometimes align with burst windows, producing the observed p99 outliers.
4) Memory fragmentation triggers host staging more often for small KV replays, shifting some traffic onto PCIe/NIC and adding jitter.

Actionable mitigations tried (short-term):
- Placement heuristics: prefer strict intra-node packing for TP slices when PP is present (reduced p99 ~40%). Tradeoff: decreases available rack-level balancing.
- Collective coalescing: batch small allreduces inside the runtime for a configurable window (10–50us). Reduced small-collective frequency and lowered p99 by ~25% in microbench. Need to validate on live traffic.
- NIC tuning: adjust IRQ coalescing and interrupt affinity for nodes running mixed intra/extra-node shards. Gains in tail but sensitive to background load.
- Buffer management: pre-allocate larger pinned buffer slabs to avoid fragmentation-triggered host staging. Reduced staging occurrences by ~70% in lab.

Longer-term changes proposed:
- Topology-aware async scheduler: incorporate link-class awareness and prefer collectives that minimize cross-hop variance. Scheduler should consider a small lookahead to avoid issuing collectives that will cross a worse-than-local hop.
- NCCL/Runtime coop: add a runtime-level signal to avoid NCCL microreconfig if a small collective can be deferred/batched within a short window; collaborate with NCCL team or upstream comm layer.
- KV cache replay rate limiter: when device is near pinned-memory fragmentation thresholds, defer replay batches or route through a local replica to avoid host staging.
- Observability: add a per-request trace that tags when host staging happens and which link class (intra-node NVLink / PCIe / NIC) a given collective used. Surface in console dashboards for customers.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- How sensitive is collective coalescing window to different model sizes (7B vs 70B) and batch shapes? Find sweet spot that reduces p99 without harming throughput for larger models.
- Can we reliably detect imminent NCCL microreconfig triggers and preemptively coalesce or postpone? Need deeper NCCL event hooks.
- Run the same trace set on homogeneous full-NVLink racks (no PCIe fallbacks) to isolate whether packetization is the dominant factor.
- Validate buffer slab approach under prolonged workloads with synthetic fragmentation (pressure test).

Immediate to-dos (owners):
- (Sofia) ship a small runtime flag to enable conservative TP placement (intra-node preference) + rollout to canary cluster. Track p99 for two weeks. Linear: TPPIPE-291.
- (Evan) prototype small-collective coalescer with 20us default window in the harness; run customer trace replay. GH: PR 1428 (wip).
- (Maya) add eBPF probe enhancements to annotate host staging events with buffer id and fragmentation metadata.
- (Liam) schedule meeting with infra networking team to test IRQ coalescing permutations on test nodes and capture NIC-level histograms.

Notes:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — prioritizing mitigations we can test quickly. We should avoid premature large architectural shifts until we can show diminishing returns from simple fixes (placement + coalescing + buffer slabs).
- There will be workload classes that prefer async overlap (latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive). The aim is to make defaults safer and expose explicit knobs for customers who want aggressive overlap.

Appendix (artifact references):
- Trace replay harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-harness/tree/topo-replay
- NCCL traces (redacted): s3://prod-bench/nccl-traces/2024-09/topo-run-03.tar.gz
- Linear tickets: TPPIPE-287, TPPIPE-291
- Draft PR for coalescer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428

Unresolved/Caveats:
- Our instrumentation still has some timing jitter (~20–50us) when correlating GPU-side timestamps to host NIC counters because of clock drift between host and on-card timestamps. We mitigated with linear clock syncing but need higher fidelity for sub-100us windows.
- Some customers run mixed workloads (short+long) concurrently—these traces amplify the problem and require per-tenant adaptive defaults.

If useful I can convert the replay results into a slide deck (short) and schedule a sync with comms + infra next week.

End of note.
